blocks.text: Why freight broker load planning feels broken

Freight broker load planning often fails because of data silos. You are likely juggling information across Gmail, Excel, and various web-based load boards. When these systems do not talk to each other, you become the bridge. You spend your day copying zip codes from an email into a browser tab. This is not logistics strategy. It is data entry.
The hidden costs of manual logistics planning

The price of manual planning is high. When you spend 45 minutes finding coverage for one load, you lose the chance to book three more. This lost opportunity is a direct hit to your commission. Worse, the constant context switching between your email and your TMS leads to mental fatigue.
Fixing your workflow without new software

items: Audit your current email templates. Standardize your rate requests to reduce back-and-forth.
Create a master spreadsheet in Google Sheets for your primary, secondary, and backup carriers.
Use keyboard shortcuts to move between apps. Press ⌘ + Tab to switch between Chrome and your email.
Set up Gmail filters to separate load tenders from carrier follow-ups.
Create a dedicated folder in your bookmarks for your most used load boards.

blocks.text: How to use your Mac more effectively for load planning

Your Mac is a powerful tool for logistics if you use it correctly. Stop relying on memory. Use Apple Reminders to track carrier follow-ups. Set a reminder for 30 minutes after you send a rate confirmation. If you have not heard back, the reminder will nudge you to call. This keeps your pipeline moving without the mental load of remembering every detail.
Moving from reactive to proactive planning

Proactive planning means knowing your capacity before the load hits your inbox. Build a list of reliable carriers for every lane you cover. When a new load arrives, check your list first. If the price is right, you have your carrier. This approach saves you from the panic of last-minute sourcing.

faq.question: Why does my freight software run slowly on my Mac?
faq.answer: Many older TMS platforms were built for Windows. If your software feels slow, check if it is a web-based version. If it requires a Windows environment, you may need to use virtualization software like Parallels or Citrix to run it properly on macOS.

faq.question: How can I reduce the time I spend on email?
faq.answer: Use templates for common responses and set up advanced filters in Gmail. By automating the sorting of incoming load tenders and status updates, you can focus on the emails that require immediate action.

faq.question: Is it better to use a dedicated TMS or just spreadsheets?
faq.answer: Spreadsheets are fine for starting, but they do not scale. A dedicated cloud-based TMS provides a single source of truth, which reduces errors and saves time on data entry as your load volume grows.
